standard.title: The crosswalk tool's own contract, mapped to the tests that hold it
standard.scope_note: Not a regulation. This file exists so the COVERED path has at least one real customer: a clause whose probe genuinely runs and passes. Keeping it separate from the MDR file avoids inflating a regulatory crosswalk with self-tests.

clauses.id: TC-1 three-state decision is a pure function
clauses.text: A clause is classified by (strength, reason, probe result) alone, with no I/O, so a reader can recompute every row.

clauses.id: TC-2 a declared gap stays green and is counted
clauses.text: A clause with strength=gap and a stated reason must not fail the run; otherwise a medical-device crosswalk, where process requirements dominate, can never be green.

clauses.id: TC-3 an unproven claim turns the run red
clauses.text: strength=carried with no probe, or with a probe that fails, must exit 1. Without this the other two states are decoration.
Probes are strings handed to the platform shell, so quoting and path rules differ between POSIX sh and cmd.exe.
clauses.reason: Only the Windows path has been exercised here. A probe written for POSIX quoting can pass locally and fail on the other platform; a containerised runner that runs both is not wired up yet.
